title: Fadell-Husseini Index: H*(BZ/p; F_p) ≅ F_p[u]
description: Formalizes the cohomology ring of BZ/p for the Fadell-Husseini index theory. Proves: principal ideal structure of F_p[u], ideal monotonicity (u^0) ⊇ (u^1) ⊇ ..., quotient dimension F_p[u]/(u^n) = n. 17 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Fadell-Husseini index theory (1988) provides a cohomological obstruction for equivariant maps. For Z/p-spaces, the index lives in H*(BZ/p; F_p) ≅ F_p[u]. This algebraic structure underlies equivariant topology results including the Borsuk-Ulam theorem.
overview.problemStatement: Formalize H*(BZ/p; F_p) ≅ F_p[u] and its principal ideal structure for Fadell-Husseini index computations.
overview.proofStrategy: Use Polynomial (ZMod p) as the concrete model for F_p[u]. Principal ideals (u^m) = span{u^m, u^{m+1}, ...} formalized via Ideal.span. Monotonicity via Ideal.span_le. Quotient dimension via AdjoinRoot.powerBasis.
keyInsights: **Polynomial model**: Polynomial (ZMod p) concretely realizes F_p[u] in Lean without abstract cohomology machinery.
**Ideal chain**: (u^0) ⊇ (u^1) ⊇ ... corresponds to powers of the augmentation ideal, encoding the filtration of BZ/p.
**Quotient dimension**: F_p[u]/(u^n) has F_p-dimension n — the basis {1, u, ..., u^{n-1}} gives the index filtration.

sections.title: F_p[u] Ideal Structure and Quotient Dimension
sections.summary: BZpCohomology namespace. ideal_chain_monotone: (u^m) ⊇ (u^{m+1}). quotient_dimension: dim F_p[u]/(u^n) = n.

conclusion.summary: 17 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. F_p[u] ideal structure and quotient dimension proved for Fadell-Husseini index theory.
conclusion.implications: The Fadell-Husseini index is a powerful equivariant topology tool. This algebraic foundation enables formal verification of index computations.
openQuestions: Can the full Fadell-Husseini index of a Z/p-space be computed formally?
Can the Borsuk-Ulam theorem be proved via Fadell-Husseini index in Lean?
Can the cohomology isomorphism H*(BZ/p; F_p) ≅ F_p[u] be formally verified using spectral sequences?
